Back in July, Holloway (28-9) defeated McGregor (22-7) via TKO in just 69 seconds, after McGregor injured his right knee in the opening seconds of their welterweight bout in Las Vegas.

Speaking at the BKFC Glasgow post-fight news conference on Saturday, McGregor, 38, once again reiterated his desire to run it back with Holloway.

"It has to be Holloway," McGregor told reporters.

"Just do the f------ thing again. Just do the thing again. The guy didn't engage once. He's the one that called for the stoppage in the fight. He said 'ref, ref!'

"He's the one stopping the fight. Imagine I just said 'yay!' and jumped the fence. I won! He doesn't want to f------ fight.

"On the one leg, he wasn't coming near me. It's so shocking and so heartbreaking to me and I'm still f------ dealing with it. It has to be Holloway. Just f------ dust it off, re-do it."

On the rehab, McGregor stated he's looking for a return potentially before the summer next year and also hinted if Holloway isn't available he could look elsewhere for an opponent.

"I'm on my way back," McGregor said.

"What's it now November? Three months I'm off of surgery. I done this injury before and returned within nine months. So nine months is pre-summer. I just want to go again and again."

"Something might happen, I don't know. But a fighter that fights me, put some respect on my name. If you're not a world champion fighter, if you've not got world accolades to your name, don't utter my f------ name."

The fight against Holloway at UFC 329 was McGregor's first appearance since July 2021 and he has now suffered serious lower-body injuries in each of past two fights, including a fractured leg against Dustin Poirier in 2021.

stories.headline: LA Galaxy miss playoffs again as Real Salt Lake gets final berth
stories.summary: Sergi Solans and Zach Booth scored early and Real Salt Lake clinched a playoff spot while eliminating the LA Galaxy with a 2-1 Decision Day victory over the Galaxy on Saturday.
stories.body:
Sergi Solans and Zach Booth scored early and Real Salt Lake clinched a playoff spot while eliminating the LA Galaxy with a 2-1 Decision Day victory over the Galaxy on Saturday.

Real Salt Lake (13-15-6) snags the ninth and final postseason berth in the Western Conference and will travel to Seattle for a wild-card matchup with the Sounders. The winner will square off against the top-seeded Vancouver Whitecaps in the best-of-three first round.

The Galaxy (11-12-11) have missed the last two postseasons after winning the World Cup in 2024.

Solans and Booth scored three minutes apart to give Real Salt Lake a 2-0 lead in the 13th minute.

Solans used assists from Noel Caliskan and defender Philip Quinton in the 10th minute to score for the 14th time in his first season in the league. Nine of Caliskan's 11 career assists and all three of Quinton's have come this year.

Booth scored unassisted three minutes later for a 2-0 lead. It was the first goal for the 22-year-old rookie midfielder in his 18th appearance and seventh start.

The Galaxy cut it to 2-1 in the 40th minute thanks to an own goal by Real Salt Lake defender Luc de Fougerolles, making his seventh appearance in the league.

Rafael Cabral totaled one save for Real Salt Lake.

JT Marcinkowski saved six shots for Los Angeles.

The Galaxy beat Real Salt Lake 2-1 at home to close out April.

stories.headline: Wings' Paige Bueckers, Azzi Fudd talk relationship on pod
stories.summary: Azzi Fudd hosted Wings teammate Paige Bueckers on her podcast and the two discussed their relationship, Dallas' season and Fudd's recovery from knee surgery.
stories.body:
Dallas Wings teammates Azzi Fudd and Paige Bueckers, the past two WNBA No. 1 draft picks, spoke on Fudd's podcast Friday about a variety of topics, including a personal life update.

"We're not together anymore; it's been a while," Bueckers said on the "Fudd Around and Find Out" podcast. "[We] share that because everybody [was] like, 'Oh my gosh, they're teammates, how is this going to work?'"

Bueckers and Fudd, who were teammates in college at UConn, said they felt the need to address their relationship status in part because of allegations it factored into the Wings picking Fudd at No. 1 in April. Fudd was chosen over TCU guard Olivia Miles, who went on to be the Rookie of the Year for the Minnesota Lynx. Spain's Awa Fam (Seattle Storm) was taken third, followed by teammates from the 2026 champion UCLA Bruins: Lauren Betts (Washington Mystics), Gabriela Jaquez (Chicago Sky) and Kiki Rice (Toronto Tempo).

Fudd, Fam, Betts and Miles were all No. 1 at different points in ESPN's mock draft in the months before the April draft. Bueckers said her previous relationship with Fudd had no impact on Dallas' decision.

"We were not together before she got drafted," Bueckers said. "She was not drafted because she was my girlfriend. She was drafted because she deserved it. She's an amazing human, an amazing basketball player. And we're still friends, we're still cool.

"We played an entire season together; we're the utmost professionals."

Fudd averaged 13.1 points but was limited to just 30 games after an injury to her right knee led to season-ending arthroscopic surgery in August. She offered an update on her health.

"My offseason's been good," Fudd said. "Lots of rehab, lots of training, lots of on-court workouts, lots of traveling. It's been busy.

"I think there's a lot I can improve on. Especially the iso game; I feel like I'm not too comfortable with that yet. I know I'm capable of doing a little bit more. Watching someone like Paige who is able to create from anywhere ... that's great inspiration for me."

Bueckers averaged 20.9 points, 4.1 rebounds and 5.9 assists, and was named to the All-WNBA second team as Dallas reached the playoffs as the No. 7 seed.

The Wings were eliminated in the first round by the eventual champion Golden State Valkyries. Bueckers said she learned a lot from her first playoff experience and complimented Golden State.

"The Valkyries' defense, I can't explain to you how tough they are," Bueckers said. "They swarm, they send bodies, they trap you, they blitz you, they're so connected. I'm glad I got to have that experience against them to open my eyes to what the playoffs are like -- the physicality, the pressure, the environment.

"And I'm proud of our season. I hated losing; I sat and was pissed about it for like a week. I reached out to [Sue Bird] about it, what was her first playoff experience like. I didn't play as well as I wanted to. But it was my first experience, going against a really good opponent, and I was learning and growing through it all."

Fudd and Bueckers also addressed the Wings' move to the 19,000-seat American Airlines Center in downtown Dallas next season after playing at UT Arlington's College Park Center, which seats over 7,000, since the franchise relocated to Texas in 2016.

"UTA was a vibe; we had a ball, we did our thing there," Bueckers said. "But definitely excited to move into Dallas. New times."

While the change in venue will lead to more eyes on Wings games, the two players said they're hoping for less scrutiny of any on-court behavior.

Both said fans shouldn't read into interactions the two have with each other or their teammates as anything other than normal team behavior. They also said they don't stand for "hate of any kind" or "tearing people down to lift us up."

"We've seen a lot of negativity," Bueckers said. "We've had stuff sent to us, stuff sent to our family, our friends. There's been some crazy things said about us. We still support each other, we're still going to be great friends, we're still going to be great teammates. All the negative things can be put aside, and you don't need to overanalyze everything."

Fudd added with a chuckle, "Also, we don't need messages [from fans] on what the other person's doing. We've addressed everything we need to, and the rest will stay with us."

stories.headline: Walsh delivers, Ponga returns and a trans-Tasman decider awaits
stories.summary: Australia and New Zealand will meet in the World Cup final after emphatic semifinal victories ended Samoa and Tonga's campaigns.
stories.body:
Australia and New Zealand will meet in the World Cup final after emphatic semifinal victories ended Samoa and Tonga's campaigns.

Reece Walsh scored a hat trick as the Kangaroos defeated Samoa 44-12 in Sydney, while Kalyn Ponga's return helped the Kiwis overcome Tonga 34-10 in Newcastle.

The results set up a rematch of the tournament opener, with both sides arriving at the decider with considerably more momentum.

Here are the biggest takeaways from the men's semifinals.

Walsh delivers when the stakes rise
The debate over Australia's fullback position has followed Kevin Walters throughout the tournament. Reece Walsh provided his strongest response yet against Samoa.

His hat trick helped the Kangaroos turn a potentially difficult semifinal into a commanding victory, vindicating Walters' decision to retain him ahead of James Tedesco.

Just as encouraging was his response to an error.

After spilling a bomb early in the second half and allowing Stephen Crichton to score, Walsh crossed himself only minutes later. He then completed his hat trick by finishing a sweeping movement involving Tom Trbojevic, Tom Dearden and Cameron Munster.

That ability to remain involved after a mistake matters as much as the spectacular moments. New Zealand will test him with its kicking game, and Australia cannot afford its most dangerous attacking player to retreat from the contest if something goes wrong.

Walsh kept demanding the ball against Samoa. With the halves creating opportunities around him, his acceleration and support play gave Australia a threat that remained difficult to contain throughout the night.

Ponga's return gives New Zealand another dimension
Kalyn Ponga returned 23 days after breaking his arm and immediately reminded everyone what New Zealand had been missing.

The fullback produced three try assists in the Kiwis' victory over Tonga, setting up Briton Nikora's opening try inside the first three minutes.

But his contribution extended well beyond the attack.

With Demitric Vaimauga breaking into the clear during the first half, Ponga made a crucial one-on-one tackle to stop the much larger forward short of the line. It was a significant intervention in a contest that remained tightly balanced before halftime.

Keano Kini had performed strongly in his absence, but Ponga's return provides Stacey Jones with an experienced attacking organiser capable of creating opportunities on either side of the field.

For Australia, the challenge now includes limiting the space available to both Ponga and Jahrome Hughes. Allowing either to operate behind a dominant forward pack risks giving New Zealand too many ways to attack.

Ponga's comeback has made an already formidable opponent more dangerous.

Hughes and the Kiwis show how to take control
The 34-10 scoreline disguises how competitive Tonga were for much of the first half.

Jojo Fifita's double put them ahead 10-6 before Dane Gagai's late try sent New Zealand into the break with a two-point advantage.

The second half belonged to the Kiwis.

With a powerful wind behind them, New Zealand repeatedly forced Tonga to work out of difficult field position. Hughes' kicking helped maintain that pressure, while Tonga struggled to find distance on the last tackle.

Casey McLean extended the lead before Hughes crossed himself, turning a tight match into a commanding advantage. Tonga did not score after halftime.

The conditions were a substantial factor, but New Zealand still had to exploit them. Their patience and execution ensured the territorial advantage translated into points.

That control will be essential against Australia. The Kiwis have enough individual quality to create tries, but their best route to the trophy is to give those players repeated opportunities rather than rely on isolated moments.

Samoa's frustration compounds a difficult night
Samoa will leave Sydney frustrated by several decisions, particularly the first-half ruling that denied Stephen Crichton a try after an aerial contest.

The Bunker ruled Francis Manuleleua had knocked on, and Australia scored through Walsh shortly afterwards. A second Samoa try was also disallowed later in the match.

Those moments deserve scrutiny, but Samoa's own errors and discipline also made an already demanding assignment significantly harder.

Australia repeatedly received opportunities to build pressure, while Spencer Leniu's sin-binning for dissent added to Samoa's problems before halftime. The Kangaroos went to the break ahead 26-2.

Leniu, so influential earlier in the tournament, also lost possession with his first carry and again after returning from the sin bin. Samoa struggled to establish the sustained pressure needed to bring their attacking strengths into the contest.

Their talent remains undeniable. The next step is maintaining enough composure and possession to make that talent count against the strongest opponents.

Australia gave them a harsh demonstration of how quickly a sequence of small setbacks can become a decisive deficit.

Australia's combinations are coming together at the right time
After several changes through the pool stage, Australia's attack looked more settled in its first knockout match.

Dearden opened the scoring with a dummy and run from a scrum, while Munster helped create Jacob Preston's try. The Kangaroos continued finding different avenues to the line, finishing with eight tries from six scorers.

Harry Grant and Munster supplied control, Walsh provided the speed, and Australia's forwards gave them a stronger platform than they had enjoyed during some of their earlier outings.

Pat Carrigan and Tino Fa'asuamaleaui made important contributions through the middle, offering encouragement after the scrutiny directed at the pack during the pool stage.

The final will provide a more demanding examination. New Zealand's forwards troubled Australia in their opening meeting, and winning that battle will be central to whether the Kangaroos can reproduce Sunday's attacking fluency.

Australia won the opener 24-22. With Ponga back and both teams coming off convincing semi-final performances, the rematch offers every prospect of another closely fought contest.

The title will be decided at Suncorp Stadium on November 15.

stories.headline: NFL Week 9: Big takeaways, questions and fantasy spin from Sunday's games
stories.summary: Our NFL Nation reporters react to all the action, answering the biggest questions coming out of each Sunday game. Here's what we learned from Week 9.
stories.body:
The Sunday slate for Week 9 of the 2026 NFL season kicked off in Madrid with the Bengals' offense erupting in a win over the Falcons. Cincinnati wide receiver Ja'Marr Chase finished with a season-high 155 yards and a touchdown on 10 receptions.

Back in the United States, Rams edge rusher Myles Garrett returned from injury, finishing with three sacks in a win over the Commanders. Browns quarterback Shedeur Sanders fell to the Saints in his first start of the 2026 season. And quarterback Bo Nix led the Broncos to their fifth fourth-quarter comeback this year -- tied for the most through nine games in NFL history, per the Elias Sports Bureau.

In the late window Sunday, the 49ers forced five turnovers in a dominant win over the Raiders. Quarterback Drew Lock led the Seahawks to a win over the Cardinals in place of the injured Sam Darnold. The Texans and Packers scored 40-plus points in victories over the Chargers and Patriots, respectively.

Our NFL Nation reporters react to all the action, answering lingering questions coming out of each game -- including how teams will approach Tuesday's trade deadline. Fantasy football analysts Matt Bowen and Tristan Cockcroft also have fantasy takeaways from each matchup.

Let's get to it with the biggest lessons from Sunday.

Jump to:

GB-NE | HOU-LAC | ARI-SEA

LV-SF | DAL-IND | CLE-NO

NYG-PHI | NYJ-KC | DEN-CAR

LAR-WSH | DET-MIA | CIN-ATL

Catch up on Thursday's game:

JAX-BAL

Green Bay 45, New England 27
Catch up on the action: Box score | Recap

Packers
Should Jordan Love be in the MVP conversation? If he wasn't before, he should be now -- especially considering the Packers have virtually no run game to help him. Love carved up the Patriots to the tune of 372 yards, three touchdown passes, one rushing TD and no interceptions, and he didn't even have to play the final nine minutes of the game. He was perfect against the blitz, and his deep throws were once again on target. It was his second game of the season with at least six completions on throws of 20-plus air yards. The rest of the NFL has zero, according to ESPN Research. Having receivers such as Christian Watson (seven catches, 171 yards, one touchdown) and Matthew Golden (10 catches, 164 yards, one touchdown) certainly helps, but it's a mutually beneficial relationship.

Trend to watch: The Packers aren't just taking the ball away this season, they're taking it early. Their 16th takeaway of the season came on the Patriots' second play from scrimmage -- an interception by safety Xavier McKinney. It was the fifth first-quarter interception by the Packers this season. They didn't have a single first-quarter interception last season. -- Rob Demovsky

Next game: vs. Vikings (Sunday, 1 p.m. ET)

Patriots
How concerned should the Pats be with Drake Maye's turnover issues resurfacing? Maye has said his commitment to owning the difference between the big play and the right play was key to overcoming his slow start, yet he lost his edge Sunday. His pick on the second offensive play reflected that, setting the tone for a day the Pats were outclassed in every phase. Maye threw three INTs in the first half and has 11 on the season. He had eight picks all of last season. The Patriots haven't had a positive turnover differential in a game this season and are now minus-10 on the year. So there is a high level of concern, especially for a team hoping to make a deep playoff run.

Most surprising performance: Christian Gonzalez was dominated. The NFL's highest-paid cornerback has seldom, if ever, been attacked as much as the Packers went after him. His primary assignment, Golden, had 150 receiving yards in the first half, the most in a first half by any player against the Patriots since at least 1978, according to the Elias Sports Bureau. -- Mike Reiss

Next game: vs. Lions (Sunday, 9:30 a.m. ET in Munich)

Fantasy football takeaway: Patriots WR Demario Douglas scored 15.2 points as he caught five of nine targets for 102 yards. Available in over 40% of ESPN leagues, Douglas has posted 15 or more points in four of his past five games, with at least one touchdown reception in three. He's a steady WR3 in the lineup. -- Bowen

Houston 44, L.A. Chargers 22
Catch up on the action: Box score | Recap

Texans
Can the Texans sustain the offensive output? There's no reason to think otherwise. When the Texans' offense is healthy, the unit is fully capable of going over the 30-point mark, as Sunday marked the fourth time in eight games that Houston has done so. Quarterback C.J. Stroud has been rolling this season, and Sunday, he tied his career high for touchdown passes in a single game (five). Texans offensive coordinator Nick Caley has put more responsibility on Stroud's plate, and he has delivered. The run game wasn't great (3.7 yards per carry), though running back Woody Marks totaled a season-high 70 rushing yards.

Most surprising performance: WR Tank Dell had his first 100-yard receiving game since Halloween of 2024. Dell, who made his season debut last week after missing almost two years of play with a serious knee injury, finished with four catches for 105 yards and a touchdown. He opened the day with a 63-yard touchdown, looking similar to his old self. -- DJ Bien-Aime

Next game: at Browns (Sunday, 1 p.m. ET)

Chargers
Do the Chargers have an OC issue or a Justin Herbert one? You can make the argument either way. As for Mike McDaniel, his quarterback wasn't protected; Herbert was sacked eight times and the offense had seven penalties for 69 yards. The unit also didn't score a touchdown until the fourth quarter, but some of that blame belongs to Herbert (13-of-23 for 193 yards and a TD) -- who threw an interception and left plays on the field. Herbert, who was replaced by DJ Uiagalelei midway through the fourth quarter, has 10 interceptions on passes of 10-plus air yards this season (the most in the NFL).

Key stat to know: The Chargers' TD drought is over. After Los Angeles went 37 drives without a touchdown, Herbert found Quentin Johnston for a 58-yard score, ending the longest such streak by any team since a 39-drive streak by the Chargers from Week 16 of 2023 to Week 1 of 2024. -- Bien-Aime

Next game: at Ravens (Sunday, 8:25 p.m. ET)

Fantasy football takeaway: Stroud's improved performance on deep throws (all five of his touchdown passes were on throws 10-plus yards downfield) has elevated him into fantasy QB1 territory. His remaining schedule is among the tougher ones, but he's throwing with a level of accuracy and upside that make him an intriguing option for managers weak at the position. -- Cockcroft

Seattle 17, Arizona 3
Catch up on the action: Box score | Recap

Seahawks
Will Drew Lock get another chance to keep his strong season going? Like he did when Sam Darnold was sidelined in September, Lock again played clean football while leading Seattle to a win. He completed 19 of 28 passes for 175 yards, a touchdown and no turnovers, though he was nearly picked on a screen pass that bounced off the defender's hands. Lock was playing through a right elbow injury and took a trip to the medical tent, which might explain a couple of wobbly throws. It's unknown whether Darnold's quad injury and cracked rib will allow him to play next Sunday. But with the way Lock has played -- and the bye in Week 11 -- giving Darnold another week off has obvious appeal.

Key stat to know: Per ESPN Research, AJ Barner became only the sixth tight end in NFL history with a rushing touchdown and a receiving touchdown in the same game. Barner got his first score on a tush push carry, which has been an unstoppable play for the Seahawks since they began using it last season. -- Brady Henderson

Next game: at Raiders (Sunday, 4:05 p.m. ET)

Cardinals
What's next for the Cardinals' offense now that Gardner Minshew II's magic didn't appear? Any magic that the Cardinals hoped for from Minshew didn't come to fruition against the Seahawks. In fact, Sunday was the polar opposite of what Minshew provided in his dynamic performance last week. Arizona's offense got to the red zone twice, which produced just a field goal. If the Cardinals' offense can't get going next Sunday, the clock on playing Carson Beck will start in earnest. Arizona has the Rams and the Chiefs coming up before hosting the Commanders in Week 12. Sitting at 3-6, a wild-card spot might have slipped through Arizona's fingers, and the future might need to be the biggest priority.

Key stat to know: On their first and last drives combined, the Cardinals had one explosive play (a rushing play of 10-plus yards or a passing play of 20-plus yards) and five plays of 15-plus yards. And on those other drives, Arizona never got beyond the Seahawks' 43-yard line. Those first and last drives led to just three points, but the big plays put Arizona in position to get touchdowns. -- Josh Weinfuss

Next game: vs. Rams (Sunday, 4:05 p.m. ET)

Fantasy football takeaway: The Seahawks' backfield continues to roll along as a committee. Zach Charbonnet had the lead (55% snap rate, 16 carries, two targets) and scored 9.6 fantasy points, but Jadarian Price wasn't far behind in usage (39%, nine and four) and had the greater point total (11.8). Price's receiving usage is interesting for PPR play, but neither can generally be trusted in a share of the rushing chores. At least a Week 10 matchup against the Raiders is favorable enough that both can be flex options. -- Cockcroft

San Francisco 38, Las Vegas 17
Catch up on the action: Box score | Recap

49ers
What do the 7-1 49ers need to do by Tuesday's trade deadline? The Niners welcomed key players back from injury Sunday, including DE Nick Bosa and WR Demarcus Robinson. But with the NFC's top seed within reach, the team should be aggressive in bolstering a roster that has already had its depth tested this season. After adding DT DeForest Buckner via trade, San Francisco is still thin at receiver and cornerback and can't afford to operate as if it will stay healthy once the currently injured players return. Cornerback, in particular, is a sneaky need, especially after Renardo Green left Sunday's game with a back issue.

Trend to watch: Aside from the punt unit, the 49ers' special teams have been an adventure for most of the season. The kick coverage group has been a significant issue of late. The Raiders averaged 31.7 yards per return, and the 49ers are giving up a league-worst 30.3 yards per kick return since Week 5. It didn't hurt them much Sunday, but it bears watching in the second half of the season. -- Nick Wagoner

Next game: at Cowboys (Sunday, 4:25 p.m. ET)

Raiders
The Raiders are unlikely to make a trade deadline deal, but should they? The best path forward for the 4-5 Raiders is likely to stand pat and evaluate their fairly young roster. At the same time, they are still in the hunt, and the talent deficiency at interior defensive line will make it hard to be competitive. Las Vegas was outclassed in the trenches Sunday. It allowed 190 rushing yards, marking the fifth time it has allowed 150-plus rushing yards in six games. The team also couldn't generate consistent pressure on Brock Purdy, who played in clean pockets for the majority of the afternoon. The Raiders should at least explore adding help in the trenches that could benefit the team past 2026.

What to make of the QB performance: Kirk Cousins put together his worst performance as a Raider. He completed 22 of 32 passes for 216 yards with two total touchdowns and three interceptions -- all of the picks coming in the second half. Cousins did everything he could to give Las Vegas hope but was responsible for sucking the momentum away. His performance will restart the conversations about when the Raiders should turn to rookie Fernando Mendoza after silencing those discussions last week against the Jets. -- Ryan McFadden

Next game: vs. Seahawks (Sunday, 4:05 p.m. ET)

Fantasy football takeaway: 49ers QB Purdy scored 25.28 fantasy points, his first game of 20 or more points since Week 3. He threw for 232 yards and two scores, plus he rushed for 40 yards and a touchdown. With a very favorable matchup versus the Dallas defense up next, Purdy should be viewed as a top-three play at the position. -- Bowen

Dallas 27, Indianapolis 23
Catch up on the action: Box score | Recap

Cowboys
Should the Cowboys make a trade at the deadline? At 4-5, the Cowboys have one fewer win than the NFC East-leading Giants (5-2-1), so they are still in the division race ahead of Tuesday's trade deadline. As tempting as it might be, owner and general manager Jerry Jones said on the 105.3 The Fan pregame show Sunday, "At this point, I don't see it." The Cowboys made their big trade already for CB Joey Porter Jr. and don't have a ton of assets to make a substantive move. Would it really make a difference? If they want to replicate 2018, when they started 3-5 and made the playoffs after trading for WR Amari Cooper, it will likely be with the current roster.

Trend to watch: The Cowboys' defense looked competent in the first half for the second straight game. Against Arizona, they allowed 129 yards and no TDs. Against the Colts, they allowed a touchdown but only 79 yards -- the fewest by Dallas in a first half since Week 18 of 2024 against the Commanders. -- Todd Archer

Next game: vs. 49ers (Sunday, 4:25 p.m. ET)

Colts
Will Sunday's loss impact trade deadline decisions? The Colts have been heavily involved in trade discussions since GM Chris Ballard was fired last month; they've already traded away guard Quenton Nelson and defensive tackle DeForest Buckner. But the word around the team Sunday was that the Colts were less likely to make a splashy deal than to do one. Still, falling to 2-7 and suffering a fifth straight loss could impact principal owner Carlie Irsay-Gordon's thinking. Running back Jonathan Taylor and wide receiver Josh Downs are among the most discussed trade possibilities, and quarterback Daniel Jones is a more remote possibility.

Trend to watch: Is it any coincidence that two of Taylor's worst rushing performances this season have come after the Nelson trade? Taylor produced 23 rushing yards a week ago at Jacksonville on 2.9 yards per rush. On Sunday, he finished with 46 yards on 3.5 yards per attempt. He has had fewer explosive runs and is dealing with contact at the line of scrimmage. He has also lost two fumbles. -- Stephen Holder

Next game: vs. Dolphins (Sunday, 1 p.m. ET)

Fantasy football takeaway: When wide receiver CeeDee Lamb is the top option in the Cowboys' offense, he can produce. The star wideout had 16 targets, caught 10 and scored 33.5 fantasy points. Let's not forget the position-leading 403.2 fantasy points he had three years ago in a similar spotlight. Tuck that away as we track George Pickens' (hamstring, shoulder) availability in upcoming weeks. -- Cockcroft

New Orleans 23, Cleveland 22 (OT)
Catch up on the action: Box score | Recap

Saints
Can the Saints' offense and special teams ever put all the pieces together? The Saints made a lot of moves during the bye week -- moving on from run game coordinator T.J. Paganetti, promoting kicker Charlie Smyth and claiming running back Audric Estime (while releasing Kendre Miller). But the issues persisted: Smyth missed a kick and the Saints couldn't score a touchdown until the last minute of regulation. Estime's 72 rushing yards and go-ahead TD with one minute left in regulation was a step forward, and having LT Kelvin Banks Jr. back will be a big boost. However, Shough was still sacked five times, and they'll need to score TDs early and often if they want to win.

Trend to watch: The Saints keep turning the ball over. Rookie wide receivers Barion Brown and Jordyn Tyson both coughed up the ball, and the team's nine fumbles are the most in the NFL. Their 15 turnovers are tied for the third most in the league (with the Colts and Patriots). -- Katherine Terrell

Best quote from the locker room: Edge rusher Carl Granderson mentioned earlier in the week that the defense had seen comments from Browns QB Shedeur Sanders that appeared critical of their defense. "We seen a lot on film, so," Granderson said before pausing. "I don't think we was motivated though. I mean, we seen him chirping. So we just came into this game ready to play, won the game on defense. I think it's disrespectful for somebody to laugh at our defense, took us as a joke. So we went out there and balled out." The Saints had five sacks, with Granderson and Chase Young combining for three.

Next game: vs. Panthers (Sunday, 1 p.m. ET)

Browns
Did Shedeur Sanders do enough to make the Browns rethink their QB situation? With Deshaun Watson (concussion) sidelined, Sanders made his first start of the season. Sanders got off to a slow start -- not unlike most of Watson's first eight games -- before heating up late with a pair of 60-yard completions in the second half and a two-minute drill to send the game to overtime. Sanders brings an element of deep-ball passing that can help Cleveland's offense. But with his play-to-play inconsistency -- his 31% success rate on dropbacks was the second-lowest mark of the season for Cleveland -- and some notable operational issues, Sanders continued to show his inexperience.

Key stat to know: Sanders had two completions of 60-plus yards against the Saints, bringing his total on such throws to three since the beginning of last season. That's tied with Aaron Rodgers and Sam Darnold for the most in the NFL over that span. Watson had one such completion this season. -- Daniel Oyefusi

Best quote from the locker room: "He's a game changer. He's always confident. He makes everyone want to play up his level of competition," KC Concepcion said on Shedeur Sanders.

Next game: vs. Texans (Sunday, 1 p.m. ET)

Fantasy football takeaway: Browns rookie WR KC Concepcion, who returned from an in-game leg injury versus the Saints, caught 4 of 6 targets for 85 yards and a touchdown (his first as a pro). And he added three rushing yards to finish with 18.8 fantasy points. With 18 or more points in two of his past three games, and dynamic ability after the catch, managers can play Concepcion as an upside WR3 in Week 10 vs. Houston. -- Bowen

N.Y. Giants 19, Philadelphia 11
Catch up on the action: Box score | Recap

Giants
What does ending a 13-game skid in Philadelphia mean for the Giants? The Giants need to be taken seriously. It doesn't matter that the Eagles are in shambles and on their third quarterback. The Giants are 5-2-1 and have a commanding lead in an NFC East they haven't won since 2011. Even though it wasn't pretty most of the afternoon in Philadelphia, they are now in position to be aggressive at the trade deadline. The Giants have the division (and playoffs) in sight. While Colts running back Jonathan Taylor has been on the radar, a starting-caliber defensive lineman might be the more likely move before Tuesday's trade deadline.

Key stat to know: Linebacker Arvell Reese needed only 2.29 seconds to sack Philadelphia's Joe Milton in the second quarter. It was the fastest time to a sack for a Giants player in the past 10 seasons when Reese got a free run at Milton and forced a fumble. It was part of a monster game for the impressive rookie, who had 12 tackles, three sacks, three quarterback hits, three tackles for loss and the forced fumble. -- Jordan Raanan

Next game: vs. Commanders (Thursday, 8:15 p.m. ET)

Eagles
Does this loss have any impact on how the Eagles will approach the trade deadline? Whatever hopes the Eagles had of making a run at the division title should be largely extinguished after their loss to the Giants. Losers of seven straight, general manager Howie Roseman can feel emboldened to make deals that prioritize 2027 and beyond. Expect the core to stay intact, but a trade or two involving players on expiring contracts would be no surprise if the compensation is right. Players who could draw interest include tight end Dallas Goedert, cornerback Riq Woolen and defensive tackle Moro Ojomo.

What to make of the QB performance: Joe Milton got the start despite being with the team for only three weeks. Predictably, the operation was rough around the edges. Milton was able to push the ball downfield at times, and his mobility helped extend some plays. But second-half struggles continued despite the change from Tanner McKee to Milton -- as did the leaks along the offensive front. The fact that the story remains the same with a different signal-caller points in large part back to coaching. -- Tim McManus

Next game: vs. Steelers (Nov. 22, 4:25 p.m. ET)

Fantasy football takeaway: Giants TE Isaiah Likely continued to demonstrate his top-five positional status, scoring 16.3 fantasy points despite a quarterback change during the game (note: J.J. McCarthy was able to return after leaving with an injury). Likely has four games of 15-plus points, and he's now second in the league among tight ends in target share (27%). -- Cockcroft

Kansas City 35, N.Y. Jets 12
Catch up on the action: Box score | Recap

Chiefs
Should the Chiefs prioritize receiver or offensive line at the trade deadline?In a perfect scenario, the Chiefs would upgrade both positions. The more likely outcome is they acquire a receiver, as quarterback Patrick Mahomes hasn't completed a pass of 20-plus air yards since Week 4, when deep threat Tyquan Thornton suffered a dislocated ankle. Plus, it might be even more of a priority after Xavier Worthy's left hamstring injury in the fourth quarter Sunday. But Chiefs general manager Brett Veach should also be calling about an OT. Second-year left tackle Josh Simmons hasn't played this season because of a lower-back injury. Right tackle Jaylon Moore also left Sunday's game with a right ankle injury.

Most surprising performance: Before this week, the Chiefs had only nine sacks, tied for the fewest in the league. But the Chiefs recorded more than half their previous season total on Sunday, sacking Jets quarterback Geno Smith five times. The last sack was significant one for defensive tackle Chris Jones, who now has the second-most sacks in franchise history (90.5). -- Nate Taylor

Next game: at Falcons (Sunday, 1 p.m. ET)

Jets
Should the Jets bench QB Geno Smith now and start positioning themselves for 2027? At some point, the Jets need to take a look at rookie Cade Klubnik, but this doesn't feel like the right time. Smith didn't play well Sunday, but he had been performing above expectations before then. Coach Aaron Glenn is on the hot seat and desperately needs wins to save his job, which is why he probably will stick with Smith until mathematical elimination. But make no mistake, this was ugly. Smith was sacked five times, squandered chances in scoring territory, and had only 89 passing yards through three quarters. He was so frustrated that he spiked his helmet on the bench.

Key stat to know: After two sacks Sunday, rookie edge rusher David Bailey now has 7.5, the most by a first-round pick in his first eight games since Pro Football Hall of Famer Julius Peppers had nine in 2002. Bailey, drafted No. 2 overall, is New York's top foundational piece on defense. -- Rich Cimini

Next game: vs. Bills (Sunday, 1 p.m. ET)

Fantasy football takeaway: Chiefs RB Kenneth Walker III scored a season-high 36.3 points, which was his third game of 30-plus points this season. Walker, who had 143 total yards and three touchdowns on 22 touches, had two subpar games this season (against Seattle and Denver), but he remains the most consistent part of the Chiefs' offense in fantasy scoring. -- Bowen

Denver 26, Carolina 21
Catch up on the action: Box score | Recap

Broncos
Will injuries in the Broncos' secondary finally catch up to them? Backup safety Devon Key's game-changing interception was just inches off the ground when he secured the ball. And that might be the margin for error for the Broncos this season. On a day when the team's starting safeties were gameday inactives, cornerback Riley Moss left Sunday's game in the second quarter with a concussion. The Broncos have already played three games this season without Pat Surtain II and four games without Talanoa Hufanga. Panthers QB Bryce Young threw three touchdowns, consistently targeting backups. The Broncos hope to have both starting safeties back after the bye, but an extended absence from Moss could hurt their nickel and dime packages.

What to make of the QB performance: Bo Nix continues to use the fourth quarter as his own personal football affirmation. After his red zone interception midway through the second quarter gave the Panthers enough momentum to turn a 10-0 Broncos lead into a 14-13 Carolina lead in the third quarter, Nix again did fourth-quarter things. His 26-yard touchdown pass to Pat Bryant II came four minutes after he had closed out a 14-play, 81-yard touchdown drive. -- Jeff Legwold

Next game: vs. Raiders (Nov. 22, 4:25 p.m. ET)

Panthers
How did the Panthers' defense respond after the DC switch? The unit, inherited by interim defensive coordinator Todd Wash this week, got off to a rough start Sunday. While a Corey Thornton red zone interception and a Chau Smith-Wade pass breakup in the end zone mitigated some of the damage, the unit allowed a pair of big TD drives in the fourth quarter. Wash's debut saw Carolina surrender 312 net yards and three touchdowns (five scoring drives). The Panthers' makeshift starting cornerbacks, Thornton and Marco Wilson -- a pair of practice squad call-ups -- had five pass interference penalties (four accepted) that prolonged scoring drives.

Trend to watch: The Panthers haven't exceeded 21 points since their Week 6 win over the Eagles. Unsurprisingly, that's also the last time they won a game. The Panthers averaged 29.2 points per game in their first five games, starting 3-2. Since that early run, they've averaged 17.7 points per game and are now 3-5. -- Mike Kaye

Best quote from the locker room: "I'm going to be honest, I don't really care about the momentum shift deal, we've just got to do our job and do what we do," defensive tackle Derrick Brown said. "Adversity strikes, right? Play football this long, adversity is going to hit. It is what it is, but we've got to execute and do our job and stop the leakage that's happening."

Next game: at Saints (Sunday, 1 p.m. ET)

Fantasy football takeaway: WR Pat Bryant II's return from IR was a fruitful one: five targets for 15.6 fantasy points, including a 26-yard score. Bryant's upside and modest usage in this game could prove useful in deeper fantasy leagues and dynasties. He's available in 98.8% of ESPN leagues and could be a worthy streamer for "bye-maggedon" Week 11 vs. Las Vegas. -- Cockcroft

L.A. Rams 20, Washington 13
Catch up on the action: Box score | Recap

Rams
Will the Rams add a receiver before Tuesday's trade deadline? Not likely. Coach Sean McVay has said he doesn't expect to make a big move at the deadline, and the Rams don't have a lot of draft capital to work with. But until Davante Adams is back from his hamstring injury, the Rams are extremely thin at WR outside of Puka Nacua. On Sunday, Nacua had 14 catches for 150 yards and a touchdown on 19 targets. The other wide receivers combined for four catches for 36 yards. The Rams are above .500, but they've struggled to move the ball consistently this season. They were 3-for-14 on third-down against Washington.

Key stat to know: In his first game back from a knee injury, Rams edge rusher Myles Garrett had three sacks, his first three since being traded to Los Angeles in June. It was his first multisack game since Week 12 of last season, when he had three against the Raiders. -- Sarah Barshop

Next game: at Cardinals (Sunday, 4:05 p.m. ET)

Commanders
How does this loss impact Washington's trade deadline strategy? Washington might be mathematically alive for the NFC East title at 2-5-1, but the season clearly continues to head in the wrong direction. So it's fair to wonder how Sunday's loss impacts whether or not they make deals. Among those players who could be attractive to other teams: pass-rushing linebackers K'Lavon Chaisson and Dorance Armstrong, who are both on expiring deals. However, Washington might want to re-sign one or both for 2027. Also, the Commanders could still add a player -- like a high-ceiling receiver with more years on his contract.

What to make of the QB performance: Jayden Daniels completed 24 of 35 passes for 273 yards and a touchdown, but Washington's lone scoring drive after the first two series was set up by an interception deep in Rams' territory. The game highlighted the need for Washington to find him more help -- from the line to the run game. Daniels' big mistake was running loose with the ball, which led to a fumble and a Rams' field goal drive. -- John Keim

Best quote from the locker room: "Today I felt like was a gut check," edge rusher K'Lavon Chaisson said. "They were running the same play all day, feeding the same person the ball all day. As a defense you've got to ... figure out how you're going to stop that and not let it happen anymore." Nacua had 14 catches on 19 targets for 150 yards.

Next game: at Giants (Thursday, 8:15 p.m. ET)

Fantasy football takeaway: Rams RB Blake Corum's recent surge in usage has created a true backfield rotation in Los Angeles. Corum scored 11.8 points Sunday, rushing for 58 yards and a touchdown on 11 carries. He has now had 11 carries and a rushing score in three straight games, including double-digit points in five straight. Corum will move up into our RB2 rankings ahead of Week 10 at Arizona. -- Bowen

Detroit 19, Miami 9
Catch up on the action: Box score | Recap

Lions
Has the Lions defense gone from a weakness to a strength? Sure, the past two offenses they've faced -- Minnesota and Miami -- were the 26th and 31st scoring offenses entering Week 9, respectively, but the unit has now stacked four solid performances in a row. Through the first four weeks, Detroit's defense was second-to-last in points allowed (31.8). Since then -- in wins against the Cardinals, Packers, Vikings and Dolphins -- they've allowed just 17.0 per game. Given the Lions' normally high-scoring offense had struggled to score in each of the past two contests, the defensive turnaround couldn't have come at a better time.

Trend to watch: Sunday marked the second straight game in which the Lions failed to score a touchdown in the first half -- their first time doing so in consecutive games since October 2022. Part of the reason for that was quarterback Jared Goff being pressured on 40% of his dropbacks in the opening two quarters. -- ESPN staff

Next game: vs. Patriots (Sunday, 9:30 a.m. ET in Munich)

Dolphins
What does this performance say about the Dolphins' defense? The Lions entered Sunday's matchup leading the NFL in yards per game with 395.4, but they were held to just 120 at halftime. Miami's pass rush, which had just nine sacks in its previous seven games, sacked Goff three times and forced him to throw his second interception of the season. Ultimately, the Dolphins' defense kept them in this game while their offense floundered and has grown immensely over the course of the season -- specifically their young players. All five of Miami's interceptions in 2026 are by first- and second-year players.

Trend to watch: For the second straight week, the Dolphins averaged fewer than 4.0 yards per carry, as Detroit's ninth-ranked run defense lived up to its ranking. After five straight games of rushing for more than 100 yards, the Dolphins have now been held under 80 yards in consecutive games. Quarterback Malik Willis has also recorded single-digit rushing yards in back-to-back weeks. -- Marcel Louis-Jacques

Next game: at Colts (Sunday, 1 p.m. ET)

Fantasy football takeaway: Dolphins QB Malik Willis -- a popular streaming pick (season-high 15.1% start rate) -- scored an entirely forgettable 3.82 fantasy points. The groin issue that was brought to light during the game severely limited his mobility. Willis needs that facet of his game for him or his receivers to have any hope of streaming utility in future favorable matchups (Bills in Weeks 11 and 17; Bears in Week 14). -- Cockcroft

Cincinnati 34, Atlanta 17
Catch up on the action: Box score | Recap

Bengals
Has QB Joe Burrow established himself as the MVP? It's hard to argue against it, especially with how he has looked recently. One week after Burrow had six total touchdowns in an overtime win over the Titans, he put on an even more impressive performance against the Falcons, going 24-of-29 for 271 yards and three TDs. Burrow completed 16 of his first 18 passes and notably threw the ball much better than he did after tallying three interceptions last week. He's enhancing his case to finally break through and win an MVP after being a two-time finalist. And WR Ja'Marr Chase also played his part with a season-high 155 yards and a touchdown on 10 receptions.

Most surprising performance: Sunday was the day running back Chase Brown was looking for. He finally reeled off his first carry of 15 or more yards and put together a couple more big runs on Sunday. A dynamic rushing attack was the biggest thing the Bengals have been missing this season, and Brown's performance could be the catalyst to fixing that issue. He finished with 57 yards on nine carries for an average of 6.3 yards per carry. Samaje Perine added 43 yards on 11 carries. -- Ben Baby

Next game: vs. Steelers (Sunday, 8:20 p.m. ET)

Falcons
Will this loss change the Falcons' approach to the trade deadline? Probably not. There has been speculation the Falcons could move safety Jessie Bates III for draft picks. Bates will be a free agent after this season. The Falcons' 3-6 record does not look good, but the reality is they are still in the NFC South race and have the personnel to win the division if they can figure out a way to turn things around. Half of Atlanta's losses are with Cooper Rush starting at quarterback or in a driving rain. It doesn't seem like the Falcons are ready to pack it in for this season, especially since this franchise has not made the playoffs since 2017.

What to make of the QB performance: There was some good and mostly not good from Michael Penix Jr. The good? He showed the ability to make plays with his legs: a career-high 50 yards rushing. The bad? An inability to push the ball down the field with efficiency en route to just 5.2 yards per attempt. He finished 20-of-31 with a TD and a pick. -- Marc Raimondi

Next game: vs. Chiefs (Sunday, 1 p.m. ET)

Fantasy football takeaway: Falcons WR Drake London is no longer a surefire fantasy WR1. London faced a favorable matchup against the Bengals then saw only five targets and scored 11.8 fantasy points. Worse yet, his rest-of-November schedule is unfavorable: the Chiefs in Week 10, a bye week, at the Vikings in Week 11 and he also has matchups with the Browns (Week 14) and Buccaneers (Week 16). -- Cockcroft

stories.headline: Lakers get 43 from Austin Reaves to beat Pistons without Luka Doncic, 121-116
stories.summary: — Austin Reaves scored 43 points as the Los Angeles Lakers held off the Detroit Pistons 121-116 at Little Caesars Arena without Luka Doncic on Sunday.
stories.body:
DETROIT -- — Austin Reaves scored 43 points as the Los Angeles Lakers held off the Detroit Pistons 121-116 at Little Caesars Arena without Luka Doncic on Sunday.


Doncic (lower-back tightness), who is averaging 45 points, nine rebounds and eight assists over his last four games, was ruled out earlier on Sunday.


Walker Kessler added 12 points and 16 rebounds for the Lakers, who had lost four straight to Detroit.


Detroit, which trailed 40-14 early in the second quarter, could have tied the game at 90 with 9:14 left, but Cade Cunningham missed the second of two free throws.


Los Angeles got the lead back to six points with 3:32 left, and a Walker Kessler three-point play made it 107-99 with 2:15 to go.


Reaves hit an off-balance 3-pointer with 46 seconds left, then clinched the game from the line.


Daniss Jenkins scored a career-high 31 points in 32 minutes off the bench for Detroit, which has lost two in a row after a 6-1 start. Kevin Huerter added 24 points, also off the bench.


The Lakers broke the game open early, outscoring the Pistons by 24 points in the first quarter. The Lakers made 16 of 23 shots (69.6%), including five of eight 3-pointers (62.5%).


The Pistons gave themselves a chance with a strong second quarter, and Jenkins hit a 3-pointer at the halftime buzzer to pull them within 61-48.


Detroit continued to shoot well in the third, but Reaves scored 13 points to keep them at bay for most of the quarter.


The Pistons were still down 14 late in the third quarter, but finished a 13-2 run with four straight layups to cut the deficit to 84-81.


Detroit trailed by seven going into the fourth despite none of their starters scoring in double figures. Huerter and Jenkins alone outscored the starting lineup 44-30.


Up next
Lakers: At Atlanta on Monday night.


Pistons: Host Washington on Monday night.
